predecessors.name: Afsharid Iran
predecessors.text: the South Caucasus lands of Nader Shah's empire, where 'semi-independent khanates emerged as a result of the lack of a centralized government' after his assassination in 1747

successors.name: Qajar dynasty
successors.text: the khanates north of the Aras, 'forced ... into submission' by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1795 and crowned Shah in 1796; Cliopatria's Qajar shape reaches 41.98 N from 1797

capitals.name: No single capital (aggregate of khanates; point is the centroid of the 1748 shape)

ledger.x: 1748: after Nader Shah's assassination in 1747 'semi-independent khanates emerged' across the South Caucasus.

1791: Agha Mohammad Khan 'marched into Azerbaijan in the spring of 1791': he sent Soleyman Khan Qajar 'to make the Talysh Khanate acknowledge Qajar authority', 'forced the Sarab Khanate into submission', 'subdued the Ardabil Khanate' and 'appointed the Donboli noble Hosayn Qoli Donboli as the governor of Khoy and…
1796: Agha Mohammad Khan is 'formally crowned in 1796' on the Mughan plain after wintering there; the page says he 'forced the local khanates into submission' (Karabakh, Ganja, Quba named).
1796: the khanates pass under Qajar rule.
1796: Zubov's Russian army storms Derbent on 10 May 1796 and overruns the khanates by mid-June 'without any resistance'.

wars.name: Agha Mohammad Khan's campaign in the South Caucasus
wars.outcome: Karabakh, Ganja and Quba submitted; Tbilisi was sacked on 11 September 1795 and the army pillaged Karabakh and Shirvan; Agha Mohammad was crowned in 1796.

wars.name: Persian expedition of 1796
wars.outcome: Russian victory on the field: Derbent stormed 10 May, Baku, Shemakha and Ganja overrun by mid-June; Paul I ordered the withdrawal after Catherine II's death in November 1796.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line separates the khanates from Iran, Georgia, the Ottomans or one another in these years; the outline follows Cliopatria.
